stage: 4I5 Immediate DirectDraw primary writes and bounded windowed screen copies (S2-50)

baseline.reason: Guest primary presentation and screen bounds only. Fresh full DDraw/D3D1-7 related regression, core fixtures/executor plus compositor and network-route tests, strict DirectDraw builds, two native sanitizer families and actual old screen/write runtime control, real XP five surface APIs in windowed and virtual flip-chain modes and dual GPU pixel/mask checks. Other guest families inherit 247-suite 4I3 full baseline; D3D8/9 and host/protocol/shader/bundle unchanged.

sources.evidence: Unlock, Blt and ReleaseDC route frontbuffer writes to ddraw_surface_update_frontbuffer. Actual coordinates and property tests are bridge implementation evidence, not a Microsoft HAL run.

reference.scope: S2-50: one primary presentation helper used by Blt/BltFast/Unlock/ReleaseDC, including current flip-chain fronts. Windowed desktop-sized primary screen copies intersect surface/dirty bounds with the application client rectangle in screen coordinates, preferring the clipper HWND; no HWND preserves existing whole-primary fallback. Failed coordinate probes skip screen copies; signed 64-bit right/bottom avoid overflow. Accepted CPU/GDI/GPU update prefixes remain committed if screen resolve/Present fails. Native actual area/screen emitter/primary helper/Unlock/DC: 23658 checks, 10800 intersections, negative/offscreen/empty/window failures, overflow, window selection, primary versus offscreen, with/without chain and accepted-prefix errors. Thirteen strict-compiled runtime mutations; old actual screen emitter and write paths combined with current helper definitions strictly compile then fail clipping; not a complete previous-source bundle. XP actual five surface APIs, both windowed 800x600 desktop and 32x24 virtual fallback flip-chain fronts: forty immediate Blt/BltFast/WRITEONLY Unlock/GDI ReleaseDC frames without Flip. One initial GDI desktop seed, thirty deterministic CPU/GDI uploads, twenty native GPU blits, forty clipped screen copies, ten guest dirty-shadow readbacks. Zero-filled CPU readback replies are used only before complete overwrites; they do not validate GPU pixels. GPU replay validates 30720 actual resolved and 30720 displayed client pixels per backend plus exact desktop visibility masks. Five physical textures created; four explicit surface destruction commands, while the known implicit back-buffer CPU/storage cleanup leak remains S2-53. Both host devices retire all GPU resources through device cleanup; real driver owner releases once. No native HAL, genuine mode-switch acceptance, game/FPS, arbitrary clipper/occlusion/thread/device-loss/ownership completion, overlay Flip S2-51 or review stages 4/5/6 completion. Host/protocol/shader/bundle and D3D8/9 unchanged.

xp.rendering: Actual DD1/2/3/4/7 Blt, BltFast, WRITEONLY Unlock and GDI ReleaseDC on windowed desktop and flip-chain fronts, no Flip call; forty presentations. CPU dirty-shadow replies are zero intent data consumed only before complete overwrites, not pixel validation. GPU replay separately validates client bounds and actual colors. Existing implicit back-buffer CPU cleanup defect S2-53 remains tracked

validationRepairs: The old screen emitter and Unlock/DC functions compile with the current helper definitions so the control can run. It fails actual old whole-desktop screen-copy bounds; this is not a complete old-bundle replay.

The first overflow mutation survived existing INT_MIN/INT_MAX boundaries. A positive window origin plus UINT_MAX client width was added; all thirteen mutations now strictly compile and fail runtime assertions.
The retained Lock native harness now extracts the actual new primary helper, and emitter stubs return BOOL as production does. Both this family and the new primary family pass ASan/UBSan.

XP dirty-shadow CPU replies are zero-filled only before complete overwrites. No pixel evidence comes from those replies. GPU replay verifies ten real guest pre-overwrite responses plus forty independent raw/display client comparisons and exact desktop masks. Initial GDI desktop seed is pinned but is not an independent color oracle.

The pre-existing implicit flip-chain child CPU/storage cleanup leak remains deliberately visible in the frozen graph: five textures, four explicit destruction commands. S2-53 is still open; this phase does not claim complete guest resource cleanup or native fullscreen-mode validation.
